name: The Floating Market — Great Lakes Corridor Food Exchange
creator: Founded by the Lakes Cooperative Traders Alliance, 2185
description: Operating on a rotating circuit of seven lakeside access points across the Meridian 88 waterfront, The Floating Market is a weekly physical food market that has operated since 2185, predating the current corponation food licensing regime by several years and thus operating under a grandfather clause that gives it unusual legal latitude to sell real and semi-real food products. The market's 80-120 regular vendors include Great Lakes fishing cooperatives, vertical farm surplus sellers, geneware plant cultivators, fermentation specialists, spice blenders, and a rotating selection of Shelf and Tier 2 food preparers serving hot food from portable units. Prices range from Φ0.50 for a synth-fish cake to Φ85 for a jar of real honey from one of the market's three licensed apiary vendors.
cultural_impact: The Floating Market is one of the few spaces in Meridian 88 where Tier 1 through Tier 3 populations genuinely intermix around a common activity, and it has produced a distinctive lakefront food culture that draws from Great Lakes fishing tradition, synthesized and real ingredients together, without the ideological weight of movements like Synthesis Nullification.
controversy: In 2219, the Lakes Cooperative Traders Alliance received a buyout offer from an Axiom subsidiary that would have converted the market to a licensed 'heritage food experience' with controlled vendor selection and entry fees. The offer was rejected after a community vote, but three of the market's apiary vendors subsequently received individual licensing pressure that many saw as retaliation.
story_hooks: One of the Floating Market's longest-standing vendors — a woman who has sold fermented lake-fish paste from the same spot for 31 years — has recently started disappearing for hours at a time during market days, and the other vendors are covering for her without knowing why.

A corponation food safety inspector has been attending the market every week for six months, not issuing citations, just watching — and the grandfather clause protecting the market has a legal vulnerability that no one in the cooperative has noticed yet.

A Tier 4 food journalist writing a 'hidden gem' feature on the Floating Market for an upscale neural-feed publication is about to publish a piece that will bring exactly the kind of attention the market's vendors have spent 40 years avoiding.
